en krykke.explanation: "En krykke" means "a crutch". To say someone walks with crutches, use "gå på krykker" (walk on crutches): "Han går på krykker" (He walks on crutches). To talk about both crutches together, say "et par krykker" (a pair of crutches): "Jeg skal have et par krykker" (I need to get a pair of crutches).

en kuffert.explanation: "En kuffert" means "a suitcase". To say you pack for a trip, use "at pakke" (to pack): "Jeg pakker kufferten i aften" (I am packing the suitcase tonight).

en kugle.explanation: "En kugle" means "a ball / bullet". To talk about a ball used in sports, such as a football, use "en bold" (a ball): "Han sparker til bolden" (He kicks the ball).

en kuglepen.explanation: "En kuglepen" means "a ballpoint pen". It is built from "en kugle" (a ball) and "en pen" (a pen), named after the tiny ball in the tip. To ask to borrow a ballpoint pen, say: "Må jeg låne din kuglepen?" (May I borrow your ballpoint pen?)

en kujon.explanation: "En kujon" means "a coward". It is an insult, so it is rude to say it to someone. To shout it at a person, you say: "Din kujon!" (You coward!)

en kuldebølge.explanation: "En kuldebølge" means "a cold spell". It is built from "kulde" (cold) and "en bølge" (a wave). To say the weather report warns about one, use "at varsle" (to warn): "Vejrudsigten varsler en kuldebølge" (The forecast warns of a cold spell).

en kuling.explanation: "En kuling" means "a gale". To say a gale blows today, say: "Der er kuling i dag" (There is a gale today). A stronger wind is "en storm" (a storm): "Der er storm i dag" (There is a storm today).

en kultur.explanation: "En kultur" means "a culture". When you talk about art, music and theater, you also use it: "Der er meget kultur i København" (There is a lot of culture in Copenhagen).

en kulturforskel.explanation: "En kulturforskel" means "a cultural difference". It is built from "kultur" (culture) and "en forskel" (a difference). To say two countries differ, use "mellem" (between): "Der er en stor kulturforskel mellem Danmark og Italien" (There is a big cultural difference between Denmark and Italy).

en kunde.explanation: "En kunde" means "a customer". It is also the first part of "kundeservice" (customer service): "Ring til kundeservice" (Call customer service).

en kunsthistoriker.explanation: "En kunsthistoriker" means "an art historian". It is built from "kunst" (art) and "en historiker" (a historian). To say you study the subject, use "at studere" (to study): "Hun studerer kunsthistorie" (She studies art history).

en kunstner.explanation: "En kunstner" means "an artist". It is built from "kunst" (art). To talk about a musician or singer, you also use it: "Han er en kendt kunstner, der synger" (He is a famous artist who sings).

en kunstudstilling.explanation: "En kunstudstilling" means "an art exhibition". It is built from "kunst" (art) and "en udstilling" (an exhibition). The opening evening is called "en fernisering" (an opening reception): "Vi er inviteret til ferniseringen" (We are invited to the opening).

en kur.explanation: "En kur" means "a cure". To talk about a fixed program of eating less to lose weight, use "en slankekur" (a weight-loss diet): "Hun er på slankekur" (She is on a diet).

en kurs.explanation: "En kurs" means "a course (direction) / exchange rate". To say a pilot changes direction, use "at skifte kurs" (to change course): "Piloten skifter kurs" (The pilot changes course). To talk about money, use it for the exchange rate: "Dollarens kurs er høj i dag" (The dollar's exchange rate is high today). A class you attend is "et kursus" (a course): "Jeg tager et kursus i dansk" (I am taking a course in Danish).

en kurv.explanation: "En kurv" means "a basket". To say you put your goods in the basket at a shop, use "en indkøbskurv" (a shopping basket): "Læg varerne i indkøbskurven" (Put the goods in the shopping basket).

en kusine.explanation: "En kusine" means "a female cousin". Danish has a separate word for a male cousin, "en fætter": "Min fætter bor i Aarhus" (My male cousin lives in Aarhus).

en kuvert.explanation: "En kuvert" means "an envelope". To tell someone to write the address on an envelope, say: "Skriv adressen på kuverten" (Write the address on the envelope).

en kvadratmeter.explanation: "En kvadratmeter" means "a square meter". It is built from "kvadrat" (square) and "en meter" (a meter). To say how big a home is, say: "Lejligheden er firs kvadratmeter" (The apartment is eighty square meters).

en kvalifikation.explanation: "En kvalifikation" means "a qualification". To say someone is suited for a job, use "de rette kvalifikationer" (the right qualifications): "Hun har de rette kvalifikationer til jobbet" (She has the right qualifications for the job).

en kvalitet.explanation: "En kvalitet" means "a quality". When you talk about how good something is, use it: "Det er god kvalitet" (It is good quality). When you talk about a good trait in a person, it also works: "Ærlighed er en kvalitet" (Honesty is a quality).

en kvinde.explanation: "En kvinde" means "a woman". To talk about a girl, use "en pige" (a girl): "Pigen går i skole" (The girl goes to school).

en kvittering.explanation: "En kvittering" means "a receipt". To ask for a receipt in a shop, say: "Må jeg få en kvittering?" (May I have a receipt?)

en kyst.explanation: "En kyst" means "a coast". To say you live close to the sea, use "ved kysten" (by the coast): "Vi bor ved kysten" (We live by the coast).

en kystby.explanation: "En kystby" means "a coastal town". It is built from "en kyst" (a coast) and "en by" (a town). The word "by" is also in "en landsby" (a village): "Han bor i en landsby" (He lives in a village).
